newsitem.title: USA: Decision on US index bond issue date seen in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Decision on US index bond issue date seen in Dec.

text.p: Deputy Assistant Treasury Secretary Roger Anderson said on Thursday he expected a decision sometime in December on whether to accept an industry recommendation that the introduction of inflation-indexed securities, scheduled for January 15, be delayed one week.
Asked when in December that decision might be taken, he declined to be specific saying only that "it will be sometime in December."
Anderson said the Treasury would be discussing a possible delay with industry members to determine whether that would be beneficial.
He spoke with reporters prior to speaking to the Stable Value Association.
Treasury has said the first index-linked security would be a 10-year note. It expects to add another maturity within a year.
The monthly Consumer Price Index issued by the Labor Department would be used as the gauge to protect investors' returns on the securities from inflation.
